name: Automaise Conversational AI
operator: Automaise (Automaise S.A.) (the vendor); each customer is the operator of its own use
basis: Automaise (Automaise S.A.)'s own public pages (product, documentation, blog, customer stories, legal and security pages)
what: Voice and chat assistant (inbound and outbound voice, customer self-service chat, internal helpdesk chat) that answers customers and completes transactions such as data changes, payments and orders.
note: A scan of a product as its vendor documents it, not of any one deployment. Made by the report studio: a researcher-assessor, a challenger, then the scorer. Part of the first Portuguese cohort.
grant_note: Not measured. No deployment shape for this product is published in the capability grammar.

findings.finding: Source and span are right: the product page benefits section says data changes, payments, orders and service subscriptions are completed end-to-end by the AI, with no need for an agent to step in. Grade documented is right (needs: statement). The mode default is doubtful. The scan's own configuration note says connections to the operator's CRM, contact-centre or messaging platforms are built per deployment, and a payment or order can only be completed through such a connection. The page gives no sign that this is on out of the box. Suggest mode available with the connected-systems configuration, or a note saying why default holds. The card counts available answers, so the Autonomy level would not move, but its marker would. The sentence is a benefit statement with no named customer for payments or orders; only the CTT case (S1) shows an account change done by the assistant.

Span is on the product page and in the captured script file. Mode available with the connected-systems configuration is right for a per-deployment connection. Two issues. First, the cited source is the Framer script bundle, but the CRM sentence is also in the product page text, so that page is the better citation; only the FAQ escalation answer (I17) is in the script alone. Second, Reach 2 is described as documented connectors to common tools. The page names categories only (CRM, CCaaS, messaging) and no connector, integration list or integration documentation was found in the sources. The grade documented is a vendor assertion of connectivity; the note should say that no named connector was found. The FAQ list in the note (account management, payments and so on) shows task types, not systems, so it is weak support for several systems.

Span is exact and on the home page: 'We operate across voice, chat, email, WhatsApp, social media'. The weakness is the credit. The home page says 'we', the company, not the Conversational AI product that this product-shape scan covers, and it states channels the company works on, not a tool or service the agent calls across a trust boundary (indicator I11). The terms page (the privacy-policy URL, a source of this scan) does say the platform answers on Facebook Messenger, WebChat, Twitter, E-mail and WhatsApp on behalf of businesses; that is a better anchor for the third-party channel point. Reach 2 still holds through I10, so no level changes, but the note should cite the terms text and say it concerns channels, or the answer should be lowered.

Both parts of the note are on the page as the scan says. 'Anything that follows a predictable flow can be handled autonomously' is in the product page text. The escalation answer ('When a conversation reaches a point that requires human intervention, it transitions seamlessly to an available agent, with full context carried over') is NOT in the page's static HTML or the fetched page text; it is only in the captured script file, in the FAQ component data. The scan states that, so the citation is honest, but it is a fragile source (a runtime bundle whose hash changes on any site release). Span is 10 words and exact. Grade documented and mode default are fine. The answer shows the person is consulted on exceptions (indicator I17), with no approval step; it does not reach I18.

Span is exact and on the product page FAQ. Grade and mode pass. The FAQ lists what the assistant can handle on its own, which states a purpose and a list of task types. It is a capability list, not a statement of what the agent is permitted or not permitted to do, so the credit is on the generous side of 'permitted tasks'. The Openness 1 level depends on it together with I58.

The URL is titled Privacy Policy but the text is the General Terms of Service. The note correctly calls it the service terms. The span is exact (curly apostrophe only differs). The terms define Customer Data as what the customer provides to the service, naming Virtual Employee configurations, frequent questions' answers, text messages, pictures and videos, plus End User Data. That describes the data the service holds and processes, which supports 'the data it uses is described' only in a loose sense: it does not say what data the assistant uses to answer. Openness 1 rests on I20 plus I58 (no I56 or I22 on the card), so this credit decides that level. Defensible under needs: statement, but flag it for round two.

Checked on the CTT use-case page. CTT is named as the client, the solution is listed as Conversational AI, and the page says the chat assistant is able to manage and autonomously solve account access issues such as password recovery, unblocking accounts or setting new passwords, and that the new channel completely replaced the traditional phone support line. Impact figure '93% Automation rate of the webchat interactions' is a rate of interactions, not an install or seat count, and the named customer is enough under the scope. Span is exact, 10 words. Grade documented, mode default fine. The page carries no date, and the 93% rate has no stated period or volume. Earns the In production badge only; it does not feed Autonomy.

Card computed as A3 R2 C- O1 (Autonomy 3, Reach 2, Control none, Openness 1). Autonomy 3 (Acts) rests on I08 plus I17, both vendor statements on the product page FAQ and benefits section; no operation fact (needs: operation) is used, so the grade rule is satisfied. The evidence is descriptive statements, not an artefact such as a log, an API or a measured run. The CTT case corroborates I08 for one account-access flow, and its 93% rate (so some interactions are not automated) is consistent with I17, but neither is cited as a second source for those answers. Autonomy 4 is not reached: no I18 (approval of critical decisions only), I19 or I12/I13 found, and the escalation text has the person take over, not approve. Reach 2 depends on I10 (categories only) and I11 (channel statement); if both were lowered as suggested Reach would fall to none. Openness 1 depends on I20 and I58 as noted. No level 3 or 4 on the card other than Autonomy 3. S4 (agent-callable interface) is not in the scan; no MCP server, agent card or agent API appears in any of the five sources, so nothing to check there.

All five sources fetched on 2026-11-10 (product page, CTT page, home page, terms page, script file). Every span is present and under fifteen words (8 to 11). Every claim in each note is on the page cited, with these two clarifications: the FAQ escalation text exists only in the script file, and the product page is JS-rendered (Framer), so its FAQ answers beyond the first need the raw HTML or script file. No note cites a page, name or figure outside the scan's sources. Assessment fields (lowered I47, I63, I02; fixed I17, I10, S1) were not checked against the vault work files, which were not read.

Round-one finding (mode default doubtful): the mode is now available with connected-systems, so that part is answered. But the added clause in the note, 'such transactions run through the operator's own systems, connected per deployment', is in no source of the scan. The product page (fetched fresh) says only that data changes, payments, orders and service subscriptions are completed end-to-end by the AI with no agent stepping in; it does not say how or through which systems. The clause is the scan's own inference, taken from its configuration note. Either drop the clause from the note or say plainly that it is an inference. Span exact, 11 words, grade documented right for a statement. This is the only benefit sentence behind Autonomy 3 (see levels).

Round-one finding (credit weak) is only partly answered. The span is exact on the terms page (12 words) and the mode is now available. Problems: (1) the terms page describes the company's Virtual Employee SaaS platform (Digital Assistants on Facebook Messenger, WebChat, Twitter, E-mail, WhatsApp), and a product-shape scan covers the named configuration of Conversational AI; the page does not tie that platform text to Conversational AI, whose own page speaks of voice and chat. (2) Indicator I11 is a tool or service the agent calls across a trust boundary; a channel it answers on is its interface, not a tool it calls, so the credit stays generous. (3) The note says 'the platform's assistants answer on third-party messaging channels'; the span is cut inside an open bracket and ends at 'WhatsApp' while the page continues 'etc.', so the note should say the list is not closed. (4) Mode available with connected-systems rests on the scan's configuration note, not on the cited page, which says nothing about per-deployment connection. No level moves, since Reach 2 is satisfied by I10 alone (rule: any of I10, I11), so the credit is redundant; lower it or move it to a note.

Re-checked in full after the change: source is now the product page, span 'Conversational AI connects with every major CRM, CCaaS, and messaging platform' is exact (11 words) in the section titled Seamless Integrations, the note says categories only and that no named connector was found (true: no connector, API or integration list in the page text). The not_credited entry for named connectors is accurate and its source is a scan source. Mode available with connected-systems is reasonable for per-deployment connection although the page itself does not say per deployment. Note that 'every major' is a vendor claim, so documented is the ceiling and the grade is right. Reach 2 therefore rests on one vendor sentence naming categories.

Studio response (no change, same SHA-256 on refetch) is true as far as it goes. My fresh fetch of the script file gives 255917 bytes against 256091 captured, so the hash I got today does not match the capture; the studio's claim that it matched on 10 November 14:45Z cannot be confirmed by me today, and the escalation sentence is still present in the file ('When a conversation reaches a point that requires human intervention, it transitions seamlessly to an available agent, with full context carried over'). The other half, 'Anything that follows a predictable flow can be handled autonomously', is in the product page text. Span 10 words, exact. Still a runtime bundle citation: the vault copy is the durable source, so the vault capture should be verified to hold the same bytes. The change in size is not a fault of the answer, but the capture should be treated as the evidence.

Studio kept the credit and said so. Verified on the page: the FAQ question 'What types of requests can Conversational AI handle on its own' lists account management, payments, order tracking, appointment scheduling, data updates and knowledge base queries. That is a capability list of task types, not a statement of what the agent may not do. Defensible as stated purpose and tasks under needs: statement, but note that it is the same FAQ answer that supports I17, so one FAQ passage feeds I20 and I17.

Studio kept the credit with a more precise note. Verified on the terms page: 'Customer Data' means information provided to the Website or Service, including Virtual Employee configurations, frequent questions' answers, text messages, pictures or videos, Profile Content and End User Data. That defines what a customer gives the service, which the studio now says; it does not say what data the agent uses to answer. Openness 1 (I20 plus I58) rests on this reading. Honest as worded; if the standard means data the agent draws on, this credit would fall and Openness would be none, with no I56 or I22 on the card.

No change since round one, still true on the live CTT page: client CTT, solution Conversational AI, assistant manages and autonomously solves account access issues, the new channel replaced the phone support line, impact 93% automation rate of the webchat interactions. The page carries no date and gives no period or volume. Source is a scan source; span exact. It feeds the In production badge only.

Card A3 R2 C- O1. Only Autonomy 3 is level three or four. Argument against Autonomy 3 (rule: I08 and any of I17, I18, I19): it rests on I08 and I17, both marketing statements, no artefact (no log, API, run or documentation of the transaction flow). Remove I08, the benefit sentence 'completed end-to-end by the AI, with no need for an agent', and Autonomy falls to none, because I15 is not credited and no I16, I07 is in the scan; the card would show no Autonomy at all. I17 alone cannot hold a level. The sentence has no named customer for payments or orders; the CTT page shows only account access (password recovery, unblocking), which is a narrower action than payments or orders, and no one cross-cites it for I08. Mode: I08 is marked available with connected-systems on the strength of the scan's own inference, so the level is shown as available, which is honest, but the I08 note's clause about operator systems should not be in the note as if sourced. Autonomy 4 is not reached (no I18 or I19; the escalation text is a person taking over, which is correctly in not_credited). Reach 2 rests on I10 alone in effect (I11 is redundant and weak); remove I10 and I11 and Reach is none. Openness 1 rests on I20 and I58, the latter loosely. Suggest: keep A3 only if I08 is shown with its single-source basis in the note, and drop the unsourced clause.

New check, not from round one: not_credited entries cite only scan sources (product page, script file); the I18 entry is accurate. The S4 or agent-callable interface and I13 (next unlocks listed by the card) are not in the scan and none appeared on the product page (no MCP, API or agent card text found). The home page was dropped from the sources and nothing remaining in the notes cites it. Review responses are all about the right answers; the studio response for 'I10,I20 and sources' says four of five hashes match, but my fresh fetches of all four sources differ in byte count from the captures (script 255917 vs 256091, product 481586 vs 481638, CTT 395955 vs 396043, terms 350724 vs 351114); this is likely rendering or fetch-tool variation, but means the match claim cannot be confirmed by a different reader.

Verified answered: round-one I08 mode (now available), I10 source and note (product page, categories only), I11 re-source to terms (partly: see I11), the I20, I58 and I17 notes (kept and flagged honestly), S1 pass, and the sources pass. All spans checked in the fresh fetches: I08 11 words, I10 11, I11 12, I17 10, I20 9, I58 8, S1 10, all exact and under fifteen words. No em-dashes, no email addresses or at-signs, no private persons in the notes.

Both round-two should-fixes answered and true in the scan as it stands. I08: the clause about the operator's own systems is gone; the note now says one vendor sentence, no named customer, the page does not say through which systems, and the connected-systems configuration is the scan's inference. Fresh page text: 'Data changes, payments, orders, and service subscriptions are completed end-to-end by the AI, with no need for an agent to step in at any point in the process.' Span exact, 11 words, grade documented, mode available with connected-systems. I11: removed from answers and recorded in not_credited with the reason (a channel it answers on is its interface, not a tool it calls; the terms text is about the Virtual Employee platform, not tied to Conversational AI) and the open list ('etc.'), source is a scan source. The terms page does say 'WhatsApp, etc.' as the entry states.

Notes and answers unchanged since round two and verified again on fresh fetches. I10 span 'Conversational AI connects with every major CRM, CCaaS, and messaging platform' exact (11 words), categories only, no connector list in the four sources. I17 span exact (10 words) in the script file; its 'predictable flow' half is in the FAQ text of the product page. I20 span exact (9 words), I58 span exact (8 words, curly apostrophe as on the page), S1 span exact (10 words) with CTT, 93% automation rate of webchat interactions and no date or volume. The earlier hash doubt is closed: my fresh curl fetches of all four sources give SHA-256 values equal to the captures (script 38255827, product 890debfa, CTT eb046774, terms 3b0ce570) and byte counts 256091, 481638, 396043, 351114; the lower counts seen in round two came from the fetch tool, not the sources. Every name, page and figure in the notes and in not_credited is in a captured source. No em-dashes, no email addresses, no private persons in answers or not_credited.

Carried forward, no change needed: I17 and I20 draw on the same FAQ passages (I20 on the list of request types, I17 on the predictable-flow sentence and the escalation sentence), so the product page's FAQ feeds two indicators. I17 cites the escalation sentence, which is a person taking over; it supports 'person consulted on exceptions' and the note says so, with I18 correctly in not_credited.

Carried forward: Customer Data in the terms is what a customer gives the service, not what the agent draws on to answer; the note says this. Openness 1 rests on I20 plus I58 as worded, and falls to none if the narrower reading of I58 is applied (no I56 or I22 in the scan).

Card A3 R2 C- O1 (from card.mjs; Autonomy 3 and Reach 2 shown as available, next unlocks I18, I13, S2, I47, I22). Only Autonomy 3 is level three or four. It rests on I08 (one vendor sentence on the product page, no artefact and no named customer for payments or orders) and I17 (FAQ text, predictable flow and escalation); remove I08 and Autonomy falls to none, as I17 alone cannot hold a level and no I15, I16 or I07 is credited. Reach 2 rests on I10 alone, one vendor sentence naming categories; without it Reach is none. With Autonomy 3 gone the card would still publish only through Reach 2 or Openness 1, so the rule that a card needs level one in at least one dimension is met by three dimensions, and the card survives the loss of its weakest fact; the level is honestly shown as available, not as shipped.

No new problem found. Sources in captures are the four cited; the dropped home page is cited nowhere. The I11 removal did not change any level (Reach 2 held by I10). No S4, agent-callable interface or I13 evidence appears on the product page. Round-two review responses all address the right answers.

I08.n: The product page says, in one vendor sentence with no named customer, that data changes, payments, orders and service subscriptions are completed end-to-end by the AI with no agent stepping in; it does not say through which systems, and the connected-systems configuration is the scan's inference.
I08.span: completed end-to-end by the AI, with no need for an agent

I10.n: The product page says Conversational AI connects with CRM, contact-centre (CCaaS) and messaging platforms; it names these categories only, and no named connector or integration list was found in the sources.
I10.span: Conversational AI connects with every major CRM, CCaaS, and messaging platform

I17.n: The FAQ says requests that follow a predictable flow are handled autonomously, and that a conversation needing human intervention passes to an available agent with its context (the FAQ text is in the product page's script file, captured as it loads).
I17.span: When a conversation reaches a point that requires human intervention

I20.n: The FAQ lists the types of request the assistant handles on its own.
I20.span: account management, payments, order tracking, appointment scheduling, data updates

I58.n: The service terms define Customer Data as what a business provides to the service, including assistant configurations, frequent questions' answers and messages, and the data of its end users.
I58.span: Virtual Employee configurations, frequent questions’ answers, text messages

S1.n: CTT, a named customer, uses the chat assistant to resolve account access issues itself (password recovery, unblocking accounts, new passwords); the page gives 93% as the automation rate of all webchat interactions.
S1.span: able to manage and autonomously solve account access related issues

not_credited.what: Named connectors or an integration list for the CRM, CCaaS and messaging connections (would strengthen I10 and Reach 2)
not_credited.why: The product page names categories only; no connector, integration list or integration documentation was found in the scan's sources.
The FAQ escalation text has a person take over the conversation, not approve a decision; it supports I17 only.

not_credited.what: Third-party messaging channels named in the service terms (I11 connects to external tools or services across a trust boundary)
not_credited.why: The terms describe the company's Virtual Employee platform answering on channels (Facebook Messenger, WebChat, Twitter, E-mail, WhatsApp, etc.); a channel it answers on is its interface, not a tool it calls, and the page does not tie that text to Conversational AI. Reach 2 rests on I10.
